## Proof

### 1. The ordinal ε₀ and a fundamental sequence for it

Recall
\[
\varepsilon_0=\min\{\alpha:\omega^\alpha=\alpha\}
      =\sup\{\omega,\ \omega^\omega,\ \omega^{\omega^\omega},\ \omega^{\omega^{\omega^\omega}},\dots\}.
\]
It is the least fixed point of the map α↦ω^α, and it is the smallest ordinal that is not obtained from 0 by finitely many applications of successor, addition, and exponentiation base ω — equivalently, the proof-theoretic ordinal of Peano Arithmetic.

A **fundamental sequence** for a limit ordinal λ is a strictly increasing sequence (λ[n])_{n<ω} of ordinals below λ with sup_{n<ω} λ[n]=λ. For ε₀ we take the *Wainer / Hardy-style* fundamental sequence
\[
\varepsilon_0[0]=1,\qquad \varepsilon_0[n+1]=\omega^{\varepsilon_0[n]}\quad(n<\omega).
\]
Equivalently ε₀[n] is the tower of ω's of height n:
\[
\varepsilon_0[1]=\omega,\quad
\varepsilon_0[2]=\omega^\omega,\quad
\varepsilon_0[3]=\omega^{\omega^\omega},\quad\dots
\]
and indeed sup_{n<ω} ε₀[n]=ε₀, since every element of the defining sup is some ε₀[n] and the limit of the towers is, by definition, the least fixed point of α↦ω^α.

Together with the standard fundamental sequences for smaller ordinals,
\[
\omega[n]=n,\qquad
(\omega^{\alpha+1})[n]=\omega^\alpha\!\cdot n,\qquad
(\omega^\lambda)[n]=\omega^{\lambda[n]}\ \text{(\lambda limit)},
\]
this assigns a fundamental sequence to every limit ordinal below ε₀, and to ε₀ itself.

### 2. The fast-growing hierarchy and the function F_{ε₀}

Define the **fast-growing hierarchy** (F_α)_{α≤ε₀} by primitive recursion on ordinals:
\[
F_0(n)=n+1,
\]
\[
F_{\alpha+1}(n)=F_\alpha^{\,n}(n)\quad\text{(the \(n\)-fold iterate of \(F_\alpha\) applied to \(n\))},
\]
\[
F_\lambda(n)=F_{\lambda[n]}(n)\quad\text{(\lambda a limit ordinal)}.
\]
All three clauses are effective: given n we can compute the ordinal notation ε₀[n], and then unfold the recursion along the well-ordering of the ordinal notation system below ε₀. Hence there is a single Turing machine that, on input n, computes F_{ε₀}(n). In other words **F_{ε₀} is a (partial) computable function**, and in the standard model ℕ it is in fact total — the recursion always terminates because the ordinal descent along the fundamental sequences is well-founded.

Concretely,
\[
F_{\varepsilon_0}(n)=F_{\varepsilon_0[n]}(n)=F_{\text{(tower of }\omega\text{ of height }n)}(n),
\]
so F_{ε₀} grows faster than every F_α with α<ε₀: for each fixed α<ε₀ there is N with F_α(n)<F_{ε₀}(n) for all n≥N. The first few values are already astronomical; the function lies far beyond anything expressible by primitive recursion or by any fixed iteration scheme that PA can justify.

### 3. Calibration theorem (Wainer–Schwichtenberg)

The fast-growing hierarchy is *calibrated* to PA in the following precise sense. Let EFA denote elementary function arithmetic (a weak base theory). The classical theorem of Schwichtenberg and Wainer states:

> **(Calibration).** For every α<ε₀,
> (i) PA proves "F_α is total", and
> (ii) over EFA, the statement "F_α is total" is equivalent to transfinite induction up to α, TI(α), for the primitive-recursive well-ordering of the ordinal-notation system below ε₀.
>
> Moreover, every PA-provably total computable function is eventually dominated by some F_α with α<ε₀.

The calibration extends to the boundary in the relevant direction: over EFA,
\[
\text{Tot}(F_{\varepsilon_0})\;\Longrightarrow\;\mathrm{TI}(\varepsilon_0),
\tag{†}
\]
because a proof that the recursion defining F_{ε₀} always halts is, after unwinding, a proof by transfinite induction up to ε₀ that every descending chain through the ordinal-notation system is finite.

### 4. Gentzen's theorem and Gödel's second incompleteness theorem

Gentzen (1936) proved:

> **(Gentzen).** Over the weak base PRA,
> \[
> \mathrm{TI}(\varepsilon_0)\;\Longrightarrow\;\mathrm{Con}(\mathsf{PA}),
> \]
> where TI(ε₀) is transfinite induction up to ε₀ for a specific primitive-recursive predicate on the ordinal notations. Furthermore PA proves TI(α) for every α<ε₀.

Gödel's second incompleteness theorem gives:

> **(Gödel II).** If PA is consistent, then PA does not prove Con(PA).

### 5. F_{ε₀} is not provably computable in PA

Suppose, for contradiction, that PA proves that F_{ε₀} is total, i.e. that PA proves
\[
\forall n\,\exists y\,(F_{\varepsilon_0}(n)=y).
\]
By the calibration implication (†), this proof can be unwound (within PA, since the unwinding is primitive-recursive) into a PA-proof of TI(ε₀). By Gentzen's theorem, PA + TI(ε₀) proves Con(PA); combining, PA would prove Con(PA). This contradicts Gödel's second incompleteness theorem (assuming PA is consistent, which is the standard metatheoretic hypothesis under which "not provably computable" is asserted).

Therefore
\[
\mathsf{PA}\nvdash \text{``}F_{\varepsilon_0}\text{ is total''}.
\]
Since F_{ε₀} is nevertheless computable (an algorithm for it exists) and total in the standard model, but PA cannot prove its totality, **F_{ε₀} is computable but not PA-provably computable**.

Equivalently, by the domination part of the calibration theorem, F_{ε₀} eventually dominates every PA-provably total function; if PA proved F_{ε₀} total, PA would prove the totality of a function dominating all PA-provably total functions, which is incompatible with the PA-provable totality of a standard diagonal function built from the PA-proof enumeration — another route to the same contradiction.

### 6. F_{ε₀} is provably computable in a second-order extension of PA

Consider **ATR₀** (Arithmetical Transfinite Recursion), the well-known subsystem of second-order arithmetic Z₂. ATR₀ extends ACA₀, and ACA₀ is a conservative extension of PA for first-order arithmetical sentences; so ATR₀ is a genuine second-order extension of PA. Its proof-theoretic ordinal is the **Bachmann–Howard–Feferman–Schütte ordinal Γ₀**, which is strictly larger than ε₀:
\[
\varepsilon_0 < \Gamma_0.
\]

The crucial second-order feature is this. Fix a primitive-recursive relation ◁ on ℕ that well-orders ℕ with order type ε₀ (the standard ordinal-notation system). The statement "◁ is well-founded" — equivalently "there is no infinite ◁-descending sequence" — is a **Π¹₁** sentence:
\[
\mathrm{WF}(\varepsilon_0)\;\equiv\;\forall f\!\in\!\omega^\omega\;\exists n\;\neg\bigl(f(n+1)\triangleleft f(n)\bigr).
\]
This quantifies over *sets* (functions ω→ω), so it is not even expressible in the first-order language of PA. ATR₀ proves arithmetical transfinite recursion along *every* countable well-ordering whose well-foundedness it can establish, and a standard result in reverse mathematics is:

> **(Friedman–Steel, Simpson).** ATR₀ proves WF(α) for every recursive well-ordering of type α<Γ₀. In particular ATR₀ proves WF(ε₀).

From WF(ε₀), full transfinite induction up to ε₀ for *any* arithmetical formula follows inside ATR₀: given a set X satisfying the induction hypothesis along ◁, well-foundedness of ◁ guarantees that the set of counterexamples is empty. Applying this to the arithmetical predicate that expresses "the computation of F_{ε₀}(n) halts", ATR₀ proves
\[
\forall n\,\exists y\,(F_{\varepsilon_0}(n)=y),
\]
i.e. ATR₀ proves that F_{ε₀} is total.

Hence **F_{ε₀} is ATR₀-provably computable**: it is computable, and its totality is provable in the second-order system ATR₀.

(Other second-order systems also suffice — for instance Π¹₁-CA₀, which is even stronger and proves well-foundedness of every recursive well-ordering, and ACA₀⁺, whose proof-theoretic ordinal is ε_{ε₀}>ε₀. The essential point is the same: second-order quantification over sets lets the theory express and prove the well-foundedness of ε₀, a Π¹₁ fact that no first-order system of strength ≤ε₀ — and in particular PA — can prove.)

### 7. Summary

- A fundamental sequence for ε₀ is ε₀[0]=1, ε₀[n+1]=ω^{ε₀[n]}, i.e. the tower of ω's of height n; sup_n ε₀[n]=ε₀.
- With the standard fast-growing hierarchy, F_{ε₀}(n)=F_{ε₀[n]}(n), a computable, total (in ℕ), but PA-unprovably-total function that dominates every PA-provably total function.
- PA cannot prove F_{ε₀} total: such a proof would yield, via the Wainer–Schwichtenberg calibration, a PA-proof of TI(ε₀), hence by Gentzen a PA-proof of Con(PA), contradicting Gödel II.
- A second-order extension such as ATR₀ (proof-theoretic ordinal Γ₀>ε₀) proves the Π¹₁ well-foundedness of ε₀, hence TI(ε₀), hence the totality of F_{ε₀}. Thus F_{ε₀} is provably computable in ATR₀.

### PROOF COMPLETE
